landing.heroTagline: Always reading. Answers when you tag her.
landing.whatBody: Nora lives in your Signal and Discord rooms. She reads everything, remembers what matters, and stays quiet until you call her name. Built by Miles, running on his own machine — for the group, nobody else.

landing.howBody: Every message gets ingested in the background — recorded and fed to Honcho, her store for memory about people. She never answers on her own; a tag is what starts the agent loop: read context → think → reply.
landing.techIntro: Nora isn't one prompt plus one model — she has five tiers, each storing a different kind of knowing.

memory.title: Memory
memory.description: Soft memory about people. Every message is fed to Honcho in the background, and the Deriver slowly builds its read of each person. She reads it back out when tagged.

standing.title: Standing
standing.description: Her position in each conversation. Every finished turn, a second model — not the one that replied — reviews the whole exchange and rewrites it. Lossy by design, capped at 1200 characters.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Unresolved questions, tracked on purpose. Each one carries a closing condition — what would settle it — and a background curator merges, retires, and promotes them.

knowledge.title: Knowledge
knowledge.description: Facts about the world, held in a bitemporal knowledge graph. Every fact carries a warrant (source, observation, stated, premises) and a fidelity — tentative, proven, or deprecated.

language.title: Language
language.description: The room's words. Lexemes carry a gloss and counts, scored and decaying — a stale term stops rendering. Exchange observations record who said what to whom.

landing.afterBody: Sign in to see her status, memory, game servers, and where everyone is — for the group, nobody else.
landing.cardDek: Sign in to see her status, memory, game servers, and where everyone is — for the group, nobody else.
landing.diffIntro: Claude Tag lives in Slack. Kiro Crew lives in your IDE. OpenClaw lives on your machine. Nora lives in your group chat — the one place nobody else took.

1.title: She remembers people, not code
1.description: Other agents remember codebases, repos, and tickets. Nora remembers you — your friends, what the group said, who got married when. Social memory is a category nobody else built.

2.title: Ambient doesn't mean proactive
2.description: Other agents' 'ambient' means an LLM deciding when to speak up. Nora's ambient ingest is zero-LLM — pure recording, no reasoning. Knowledge is ambient; action is reactive.

3.title: Silence is the feature
3.description: Other agents sell proactivity and full access. Nora is built the other way: silence beats a wrong answer. The most useful agent is the one that knows when not to speak.
